g1.label: 1. big packs and deals: this ___ people buying more than they can eat
g1.why: The deals are the cause and over-buying the effect: cause + “leads to” + effect.

g2.label: 2. people throw food away ___ a “best before” date
g2.why: “Due to” is followed by a noun phrase (a date); “because” would need a full clause.

g3.label: 3. busy working lives ___ meals are often not planned
g3.why: “Mean that” + clause gives a consequence; “mean to” means “intend to”.

g4.correct: To address the problem of large packs
accept: To address the problem of large packs
g4.label: 4. ___, supermarkets could sell more loose fruit
g4.why: This solution answers the first cause, so it says which problem it addresses.

g5.label: 5. ___ labels explained the difference, fewer products would be thrown away
g5.why: Second conditional for an imagined solution: if + past simple, … would + verb.

g6.label: 6. teaching these skills, which ___ less waste at home
g6.why: The skills are the cause and less waste the effect: cause + “result in” + effect.

g1.label: 1. Heavy traffic ___ air pollution
g1.why: The cause (traffic) comes first, so use “leads to” before the effect.

g2.label: 2. Air pollution ___ heavy traffic
g2.why: The effect comes first, so use the passive “is caused by” before the cause.

g3.label: 3. Flights were cancelled ___ the storm
g3.why: “The storm” is a noun phrase, so “due to”; “because” needs a full clause.

g4.label: 4. Flights were cancelled ___ there was a storm
g4.why: “There was a storm” is a full clause, so “because”; “due to” needs a noun.

g5.label: 5. Prices rose sharply. ___, many families spent less
g5.why: A linker that starts a new sentence about the effect: “As a result,”.

g6.label: 6. Lack of sleep can ___ poor concentration
g6.why: The cause comes first: cause + “result in” + effect.

g7.label: 7. Poor concentration in class can ___ staying up too late
g7.why: The effect comes first: effect + “result from” + cause.

g8.label: 8. The rise in obesity is partly ___ to a lack of exercise
g8.why: “Be due to” + noun names a cause: is partly due to a lack of exercise.

g1.correct: Local councils could run free weekly clubs where older people can meet.
accept: Local councils could run free weekly clubs where older people can meet.
g1.label: 1. Cause: older people live alone and rarely go out
g1.why: Clubs give them a reason and a place to meet others, so this fixes the cause.

g2.correct: Cities could build more affordable housing near business districts.
accept: Cities could build more affordable housing near business districts.
g2.label: 2. Cause: young people cannot afford to rent near work
g2.why: Cheaper homes near work answer this cause directly; cinema tickets and holidays do not.

g3.correct: Parents and schools could set daily screen-time limits and plan outdoor activities.
accept: Parents and schools could set daily screen-time limits and plan outdoor activities.
g3.label: 3. Cause: children spend hours on screens, not outside
g3.why: It cuts screen time and gives an outdoor alternative; more computers would make it worse.

g4.correct: Supermarkets could sell more loose fruit and vegetables.
accept: Supermarkets could sell more loose fruit and vegetables.
g4.label: 4. Cause (Exercise A): large packs lead to food being thrown away
g4.why: Loose food lets shoppers buy only what they need; label print size is a different cause.

g5.correct: Bus lanes could be added so that buses are quicker than cars.
accept: Bus lanes could be added so that buses are quicker than cars.
g5.label: 5. Cause: people drive short trips because buses are slow
g5.why: Faster buses remove the reason for driving; cheaper parking would encourage more driving.

g6.label: 6. Review (Discussion Essay): ___ of the plan point out …
g6.why: “Critics … point out” reports the other side — from the Discussion Essay exercise.

g7.label: 7. Review (Opinion Essay): ___ the course was difficult
g7.why: A full clause follows (the course was difficult), so “although”, not “despite” — from the Opinion Essay exercise.
